residencies.name: Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS) International Creator Residency

eligibility.eligibility_notes: From the 2027 Application Outline PDF: '(1) Resides outside of Japan (2) Has 5 years or more of experience in the fields of visual arts, design or architecture (3) Has sufficient ability to communicate in English (4) Independent and capable of working and living on his/her own (5) Creators working as a duo are also eligible (6) Students are ineligible (except for Ph.D. candidates)'. No nationality restriction stated, so an India-based artist meets the residence rule. FAQ Q21: 'Participation as a collective is not accepted. Applying as an individual or a duo artist is acceptable.' A duo must have done at least one project together. Anyone who has done this programme before cannot reapply (FAQ Q2). Two letters of recommendation from art or cultural institutions or professionals are required. career_stage set to null because TOKAS uses no stage label; the hard rule is 5+ years of experience, and it describes targets as 'distinguished and highly motivated creators'.

funding.stipend_detail: PDF section 3: 'Living expenses (per diem): JPY 4,200 (consumption tax excluded) per day' plus 'Fee for work/project: JPY 300,000 (consumption tax excluded)'. 'Income tax (20.42%) will be deducted from the above amounts'. My own arithmetic, not a TOKAS figure: the per diem comes to about JPY 382,000 to 386,000 for one 3-month period before tax. A duo gets living expenses and the fee for one person only.
funding.materials_budget: No separate materials budget is listed. The JPY 300,000 fee for work/project is the only production money stated.
funding.application_fee: None stated in the 2027 outline PDF or the FAQ
artist_pays: Accommodation and travel elsewhere in Japan ('We will not provide any financial support for additional accommodation and travel expenses elsewhere in Japan')
Any family or partner costs (they cannot stay at the residency, FAQ Q20)
20.42% income tax, deducted from the amounts paid

discipline.thematic_constraint: None. Fields are 'visual arts (drawing, installation, painting, performance, photography, media art, sculpture, sound art, video, etc.), design, architecture'. 'Mixed media' is not named, but the list is open-ended and names installation and sculpture explicitly.

residencies.deadline_notes: CLOSED. The 2027 call ran from 19 May 2026 to 16 June 2026, 18:00 JST (PDF section 6). Final results are due on the TOKAS website by early October 2026. The Open Call page currently says 'Currently no open calls', and no 2028 call has been announced. The TOKAS schedule page lists this programme's open call as usually running 'May to June', but also says 'This schedule may be changed', so no 2027 date for the 2028 cycle is confirmed.
residencies.duration: 3 months: early May to end July 2027, early September to end November 2027, or early January to end March 2028. 6 creators in total, 2 per period (tentative).
residencies.notes: Best money of the three, and installation and sculpture are explicitly in scope. Main blocker for an early-career artist: the hard requirement of 5 or more years of experience, plus two institutional recommendation letters. Facilities (PDF section 11 and the residency page): a single room of 25 sq m with kitchen and bath, plus two SHARED studios of 125 sq m and 48 sq m, a networking room and a library. No workshop, tools, woodshop, metal or ceramics equipment is listed. Condition 5 says 'Do not conduct any activities that would make big noise or vibration in TOKAS Residency', which limits fabricating glass vitrines or large work on site. The OPEN STUDIO is the only official presentation, and a comprehensive report is required. No commercial or profitable activity is allowed during the residency. The programme itself depends on the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture board approving its 2027 annual plan by end of March 2027. Visa handling for Indian passport holders is not described. Confirm separately.

cautions: Requires 5 or more years of practice and two recommendation letters from institutions or professionals.

Capable of communicating in English or Japanese.' The call is open 'for both individuals and groups'. funding.application_fee: None stated (checked the 2026 English call and the 2027 English and Japanese calls)

residencies.deadline_notes: No call open to a visual artist right now; the date above is the last visual-arts deadline. AIR 2026 Visual Arts ran 30 June to 31 August 2025, 23:59 JST, and is marked CLOSED. The current cycle, AIR 2027, is Performing Arts only. It ran 30 June to 31 July 2026, 18:00 JST, and is marked 'Application Closed', with results due late November 2026. No AIR 2028 Visual Arts call is listed. Going by the alternation sentence alone, the next visual arts call would be AIR 2028, probably in summer 2027 (KAC says the application period is 'typically scheduled for the summer'). Which studio a resident gets is not stated. No woodshop, metal, ceramics or kiln is listed. Studio rules: use may be restricted if 'noise, foul odor, etc.' disturbs others, 'equipment, etc., must be prepared and borne by the user', and vehicle loading must be arranged with the office. Residents must run public exchange projects and submit a report. Visa handling is not described. And no call is currently open in his discipline.

residencies.location: 77 Hanadacho Takagi, Himeji-shi, Hyogo 671-0256 (Takagi leather district, Himeji)

eligibility.eligibility_notes: 2027 call (English): 'Individual artists, designers, or creators, or artist duos currently engaged in creative practice. All disciplines are welcome.' 'There are no restrictions regarding age, nationality, or cultural background.' 'Applicants must be able to communicate in either Japanese or English.' The Japanese version matches: 年齢、国籍、バックグラウンドは問わない. No experience minimum or career-stage label is stated, and the Japanese page says no prior leather experience is needed. Solo applicants are fine; groups larger than a duo are not addressed.

funding.stipend_detail: 2027 call: 'International artists: Up to JPY 150,000 per month' (Japanese artists up to JPY 250,000). Japanese original: 海外アーティスト：1ヶ月/150,000円を上限. Official caveat: the grant is 'not a living allowance. It is intended solely to support artistic production.' and 'Living expenses are not provided during the residency.' An older L-AIR apply page (2024 dates) quoted 'up to 250,000 yen/1,500 USD per month'; the 2027 call supersedes that, and international artists now get the lower cap.
funding.materials_budget: Leather and other production materials are provided free (2027 call: 'leather/production materials'). The monthly grant is production-only.
funding.application_fee: None stated in the 2027 English or Japanese call. Apply by email to info@l-air.or.jp, subject 'L-AIR Artist Apply'.
artist_pays: All living expenses, food included ('Living expenses are not provided during the residency')
Health, accident and any other insurance ('Artists are responsible for obtaining their own health insurance, accident insurance...')
Any specialised tools beyond the standard leather equipment
Travel beyond one round trip. 'The organizer will reimburse one round-trip journey', by 'the most reasonable and economical route using public transportation', repaid after arrival against receipts.
Visa is not addressed in the call (unverified)

discipline.thematic_constraint: HARD MATERIAL CONSTRAINT: 'Creation of works using leather as the primary material'. 'All works created using leather materials provided during the residency will be donated to L-AIR' (for its archive exhibition).

residencies.deadline_notes: OPEN (2027 call posted 6 August 2026). 'Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Applicants may apply for any season at any time.' Per-season deadlines: Season 1 (4 Jan to 28 Mar 2027) by 30 Sep 2026; Season 2 (1 Apr to 27 Jun 2027) by 30 Nov 2026; Season 3 (1 Jul to 26 Sep 2027) by 1 Mar 2027; Season 4 (1 Oct to 19 Dec 2027) by 31 May 2027. The nearest deadline (Season 1) is 20 days from today.

residencies.notes: Open to him, currently accepting applications, and it pays a monthly grant, but the fit is conditional. His containment, vitrine, glass-box and hyperreal figurative work would have to be made mainly in LEATHER. Leather can suit surreal figurative work and scale distortion, but no glass or vitrine fabrication is described. Every piece made with L-AIR's leather is donated to L-AIR, so he keeps none of it. The grant is production-only, so living costs come out of his own pocket. Facilities: a converted leather factory with workshops 1 to 4, private bedrooms, an exhibition gallery and shared living areas. The studio has 'standard leatherworking equipment and machinery'; specialised tools must be brought, Wi-Fi is available, no computers are supplied, and artists clean their own space. An older, outdated apply page listed glass, ceramics and woodworking among priority fields, but the 2027 call does not repeat this. Obligations: open studio, final presentation or exhibition, at least one exchange programme, progress reports at 1 week, 1 month and 2 months, and cooperation with documentation and media. Visa handling is not described.
residencies.money_summary: Up to JPY 150,000/month production grant plus housing, studio, one return trip, free leather
residencies.style_fit_reason: Leather must be the primary material, which pulls away from his glass, plaster and vitrine vocabulary, though leather can carry surreal figurative work.

funding.stipend_detail: ANSWERED: a VSC fellowship is a fee reduction, not a stipend, except for a named handful that are not open to this client. Official fees page: 'Through the generosity of individual donors and foundation partners, Vermont Studio Center is able to ensure a full or partial fellowship for every attendee. All fellowships are awarded through a competitive process. VSC awards full fellowships to 35% of residents and partial fellowships to all accepted applicants. The fee asked of partial fellowship recipients varies by duration of session: $2,700 for two weeks / $3,825 for three weeks / $4,950 for four weeks. A 10% discount on these fees is available to residents who elect to share a bathroom with one other resident, subject to availability.' A full fellowship therefore means paying nothing rather than being paid. Official fellowships page: 'There are no eligibility requirements for a VSC Fellowship, as recipients are selected solely on the merit of their work' - and the VSC Fellowship itself carries no cash. SOME named fellowships do add cash on top, but every one of them is restricted: 'HEDDA STERNE FELLOWSHIP Supports a female-identifying visual artist for a two-week residency. This Fellowship includes a $1,000 stipend.'; 'LATIN AMERICAN AND CARIBBEAN ARTIST FELLOWSHIP ... includes a $1,000 stipend.'; 'HARPO FOUNDATION NATIVE AMERICAN FELLOWSHIP Supports exceptional US-based Native American visual artists ... This award includes a $500 travel stipend.'; 'QUEENS COLLEGE CUNY FELLOWSHIP ... By invitation only.' The one stipend-bearing visual-arts fellowship with no stated nationality, gender or institutional bar is: 'TROUT LILY FELLOWSHIP Supports a visual artist with financial need attending a three-week residency. This fellowship includes a $1000 stipend.' There is no published application route or eligibility detail for Trout Lily beyond that line.
